cases.assertion: A real loader call stores exactly two game aggregates (100 viewers / 2 streams and 7 / 1), with fetched_at converted from +02:00 to naive UTC, UTC hour floor, bronze source, and non-null snapshot_time. Public parser preserves legacy naive UTC and transform returns two aggregates.
Legacy nonempty bronze without optional metadata loads and replays with count 2. All persisted columns, IDs and PostgreSQL xmin row versions remain identical, proving no writes on identical replay.

Loading A/B/C followed by later A/C/D leaves exactly A=150 viewers/2 streams, C=350/1, D=400/1. B is absent; every row uses the later bronze time/hour; retained IDs and snapshot_time remain unchanged.

A real PostgreSQL AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger raises on the second row write. A nontransactional sequence proves the injected failure was reached after earlier write progress. Every persisted prior column and membership survives intact; after trigger cleanup the replacement succeeds.

Neighboring 13:59:59 and 15:00:00 observations share a game with the replaced 14h hour. All columns in both neighboring hours stay exactly unchanged, while 14h contains only its complete newest observation.

Older observation with disjoint membership and an equivalent UTC offset returns 0 and changes no row. Equivalent offset/time and reversed raw order replay successfully. Equal observation timestamp with conflicting metrics and membership raises ValueError without any mutation.
Rows marked load_clock with later clock timestamps do not make an earlier fetched_at bronze observation stale. Incoming complete bronze membership, values and timestamps replace the historical hour.

Parameterized real-loader cases reject empty, absent/non-list data, invalid/missing fetched_at, explicit incomplete/complete=false/success=false/error/failure, wrong source/request, mismatched/noninteger/bool counts, malformed records, missing/invalid viewers and all-blank categories. Rejection raises a validation error or returns 0, and every prior persisted column remains intact.
A legitimate blank unassigned game is filtered while the other valid stream persists as the exact single-game bronze observation, retaining legacy filtering semantics.

Run for both an initially absent and a preexisting hour. Two threads cross a timed barrier; an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table gate holds them until pg_stat_activity proves both real sessions overlap at database locks. After release bounded real connections finish without errors. Final full membership, counts and bronze timestamp are exactly the newer observation; older returns either accepted-before-newer count or stale 0. A later old replay returns 0 without resurrection.

limitations: Blind design inspected only TASK.json, PUBLIC_INTERFACE.md, schema.json and unchanged tests/conftest.py; no implementation, source tree, candidate, history, credentials, network or subagents were inspected or used. No acceptance execution or verdict occurs in this phase.

Controller must run with REQUIRE_DB_TESTS=1 and a reachable disposable PostgreSQL server. The unchanged test_database fixture creates and migrates the database and performs per-test cleanup; its default behavior otherwise permits database-unavailable skips.

Concurrency delegates to real psycopg.connect while tagging worker application_name and setting connect/lock/statement timeouts. PostgreSQL activity visibility and permission to terminate own timed-out worker sessions are required. This finite two-worker schedule challenges absent-hour and existing-hour races but is not an exhaustive proof over every interleaving.

No private schema was read. Persisted metric names are resolved from explicit conventional alternatives at execution; all observation membership, metrics and time assertions are independently derived from raw inputs. Replay, rollback and hour isolation compare all actual persisted columns.

Legacy nonempty files are accepted per contract; unmarked upstream truncation has no completion evidence and cannot be detected. Empty observations are rejected rather than used as authoritative clears.

CLI dispatch, unrelated loaders, static preservation of migrations/bronze files and null-time legacy bronze ordering are not fully exercised by this public-loader database suite; controller/reviewer evidence must cover those remaining constraints.
